title: eternal: Salt, stone and golden hour
logline: Late light on wet stone. In just under 95 seconds the film moves from the feeling of eternal's new direction, 'Salt, stone and golden hour', through its rules, stories, colour, type and motion, shows the direction already running on the built storefront on desktop and mobile, and ends on the wordmark and the promise.
rationale: The owner has to feel that this is eternal and believe it is already built, so the film opens on what they already love: their bottle on wet stone at golden hour, signed first by the e∞ mark in one stroke and then named in the direction's own words. Seven seconds in, the same water keeps moving inside a browser window while the real homepage settles over it — the site's own scrim, header, headline and buttons over live water — beside the board's line written for a Cairo house. From there everything is seen as applied, not proposed. The four principles each get an unhurried slot in the site's own 5/7 editorial layout, each carried by a picture from the same hour; the last principle becomes the hero bottle's own colour world, Wayne, which widens into its tale without a cut on the right of the frame. A second tale goes full-bleed to give the film its emotional core. Then the house's structure (three lines, each photo arriving from its line tone), the colour system (the 70/20/6/4 ratio as the picture, then one world per scent, honestly labelled 'proposed' where they are), the two typefaces set in real brand lines, and motion named as a rule of the direction: 'One thing at a time.' while the mark draws alone, 'Light, not decoration.' while a photograph rises out of its colour. The storefront returns in depth — tales and moods in a quiet browser, then two phones — and the film closes where it began, in the golden hour, on the wordmark and 'Some things are never meant to fade.', held as the end card. Every cut is a crossfade, a soft light edge or a dip through Linen, so the film demonstrates the motion direction while presenting it.
audioNote: Designed silent; every idea reads without sound. If a bed is added: one continuous, beatless ambient piece around 60 BPM — sparse felt piano over a warm low pad, with a faint distant sea wash only under scenes 01, 02 and 11. No percussion, risers, whooshes or hits; nothing synced to cuts. Mix low (about −22 LUFS integrated) so it sits under conversation in the meeting, and fade it over the last 2 s while the end card holds.

scenes.notes:
CONVENTIONS FOR EVERY SCENE. (a) 'Rise' = opacity 0→1 while translateY goes from +24 px (display type, wordmark) or +16 px (eyebrow, body, caption, numeral, chips, devices) to 0, over 600 ms (R.rise). 'Exit' = opacity 1→0 over 320 ms with R.ease.exit, no movement. (b) holdUntil = the moment the exit starts; when it equals the scene end, the text holds and the next scene's transition carries it off. Never fade a whole scene out at its end. (c) Every specified line is its own R.text block with white-space: nowrap at the stated (x, y); never rely on box-width wrapping or
(R.splitWords rebuilds from textContent). Word staggers run across lines in reading order. (d) FILM FRAME BLENDING, wherever the hero film appears: build two R.film images A and B in the same rect; A shows film.at(τ), B shows film.at(τ + 1/24); B sits above A with opacity frac = τ·24 − Math.floor(τ·24 + 1e-6). Apply identical transforms to both. Deterministic, no speed change; check with preview --strip across the loop seam (τ ≈ 5.54). (e) GRAIN: the runtime draws one full-frame grain at the highest value of all active scenes, above the dip overlay. The 'grain' field is the peak; implement each scene's grain as the function in its notes via R.scene(slug, { grain: (t) => … }) — the notes are the source of truth. Scene 01: t < 7.0 ? 0.035 : max(0, 0.035 × (1 − (t − 7.0)/0.6)), i.e. 0 from 7.6 s, so scene 02's Linen stays clean. (f) R.mark's stroke is in viewBox units: rendered px = stroke × width/96. Always draw the mark with R.drawMark, never a custom path order. reel/assets/img/home-hero.jpg equals film frame 1; poster or fallback only. Scene 02 continues this film's clock with τ = 7.0 + t.

scenes.title: Four principles

scenes.title: Three lines, one house
scenes.purpose: Show the house's structure at a glance: three lines, each with a person seen from behind, its own tone and its audience. Each photo arrives from its line tone, just as images load on the site.
scenes.visual: BEAT A (0.6–3.42 s): Linen with the title only, one line at (120, 479), vertically centred. BEAT B (from 3.5 s): a full-bleed triptych of three portrait panels, each 638×1080, separated by 3 px Linen gaps: panel 1 x 0–638, panel 2 x 641–1279, panel 3 x 1282–1920. Each panel is a flat field of its line tone: Blush clay #E3CFC4, Sea slate #1F3F50, Bone #E9E4D3. Each photo sits in the TOP 638×850 of its panel (y 0–850), object-fit cover (the 1856×2304 sources render 684.7×850, about 47 px of width cropped): panel 1 reel/assets/img/line-eterna.jpg (a woman in a linen dress walking away through a stone arch into an olive garden), object-position 42% 50%; panel 2 line-eterno.jpg (a man from behind at a sea wall under a lavender dusk sky), 50% 50%; panel 3 line-eternal.jpg (a couple from behind on a stone terrace above the sea), 60% 50%, which keeps the couple at least 25 px from the panel's right edge at full push and crops the dark sliver on the source's right edge. Every photo starts at base scale 1.04 (this trims line-eterno's thin white border) and pushes 1.04→1.07 from its fade to the scene end, around its box centre (319, 425) (R.ease.inOut). All three figures stay whole above y 850; eterna's feet sit near y 715 at full push. The bottom 230 px of each panel (y 850–1080) is the tone field itself, which acts as the band that carries the text. There is no separate band element, gradient or border. In each band, text is inset 120 px from the panel's left edge and the tone caption is right-aligned 120 px from the panel's right edge, so all text stays inside x 120–1800.

scenes.title: Colour
scenes.purpose: Show the palette as a discipline, then the idea that sells. First the ratio: neutrals do the work, Linen is most of every page, and Golden hour is a sliver. Second, each scent owns one colour world, honestly labelled where it is still a proposal.
scenes.visual: The eyebrow 'Colour' at (120, 112) stays through both beats. BEAT A (0–4.92 s): the title 'Neutrals do the work.' at (120, 144). RATIO BAR: one bar at x 120–1800, y 292–532 (1680×240), four flat segments with no gaps: Linen #F3EFE7 70 % (x 120–1296), Night #171614 20 % (x 1296–1632), Sand #E4D9C5 6 % (x 1632–1732.8), Golden hour #B97A2B 4 % (x 1732.8–1800). A 1 px Dune #CDBFA5 outline runs around the whole bar, so the Linen segment reads as part of it on the Linen ground; that it looks mostly empty is the point. Each segment carries its share as a numeral 16 px in from its left edge, top at y 476 (listed below). The bar, its outline and its numerals form one layer. Under the bar at (120, 552) is the board's ratio line. SWATCH ROW: labels 'Neutrals' at (120, 660) and 'Accents' at (1432, 660). Chips are 184×140 at y 696–836, with no gaps inside a group. The neutrals sit at x = 120 + 184·i (Linen, Paper, Sand, Dune, Stone, Ash, Night; group x 120–1408). After a 24 px gap come the accents: Golden hour at x 1432 and Deep sea at x 1616 (ends at 1800). A 1 px Dune outline surrounds each group, plus a 1 px Dune rule at x 304 between the Linen and Paper chips. Under each chip, at the chip's x: its name at y 852 (Cormorant Garamond 500, 28 px, Night) and its hex at y 888 (Instrument Sans 500, 18 px, tabular, Ash). BEAT B (5.0–10.0 s): the heading 'Colour worlds — one per scent' in the title slot, and a 5×2 grid of flat colour-world tiles, each 316.8×328 with 24 px gutters. Columns sit at x 120, 460.8, 801.6, 1142.4 and 1483.2; rows at y 284 and 636 (the grid ends at y 964). Each tile is a flat field of the world's first colour, with a 56×56 chip of its second colour at the top-right (x = tile x + 236.8, y = tile y + 24). At the bottom-left, 24 px in: the scent name with its top at tile y + 232 (Cormorant Garamond 500, 34 px, line-height 1.1), and directly under it the status with its top at tile y + 276 (Instrument Sans 500, 20 px, full opacity). No hex values appear on the tiles. Text is Linen on the dark worlds (Shadow of the Sea, Wayne, Sapphire, Enzo 1898) and Night on the others. The Linen-world tile gets a 1 px Dune border. No packshots or bottles are drawn. In the texts below, ' | ' separates stacked lines and is never rendered.

scenes.notes: All names, hex values and the ratio line are verbatim from the direction board. World names use the site's title case. The 'from the packshot' and 'proposed' statuses are mandatory: eight of the ten worlds are proposals for the packaging team, and the film must not present them as final. Hex pairs are deliberately off the tiles: the chip shows the second colour, and beat A carries the system's hex values. Line labels are also left off the tiles. No packshots and no product cards; do not use the shop capture (prices, badges, empty cards). Grain 0. Conventions as in scene 01.

scenes.title: Typography
scenes.purpose: Let the client hear the type's voice at size, in real brand lines: a calligraphic serif for what should be felt, and a quiet, narrow sans for everything that sells.

Row 3 (y 720–826), left: the UI role label and two real site buttons with radius 0. The primary button is a Night #171614 fill, 320×64 at (120, 762), with 'Shop the collection' centred in Linen. The secondary is transparent with a 1 px Night border, 260×64 at (464, 762), with 'Find your scent' centred in Night. Row 3, right, from x 1000: the Eyebrow role label and an eyebrow specimen. The rest is generous empty Linen.

scenes.title: Motion
scenes.purpose: Name motion as part of the direction, not just something the film does. Two of the motion board's six rules each appear beside their own demonstration: the mark drawing alone (the site's loader), then a photograph rising out of its colour world (how every image loads on the site).
scenes.background: Linen #F3EFE7, with a #2B2A28 panel on the right
scenes.visual: Linen ground in the 5/7 asymmetry. RIGHT panel: x 800–1920, y 0–1080 (1120×1080), bleeding off the right, top and bottom, radius 0, overflow hidden. It is a flat field of #2B2A28, the site's own After dark colour (its placeholder wash in content/taxonomy.ts). Inside it, bottom to top: (a) the e∞ mark, R.mark(panel, {x: 440, y: 480, width: 240, color: Linen #F3EFE7, stroke: 3}) — panel-local; stage x 1240–1480, y 480–600, centred on the panel's centre (1360, 540); stroke 3 renders 7.5 px, the same mark as scene 01; (b) reel/assets/img/mood-after-dark.jpg (resin and a glowing incense stick on dark stone in low warm light, a thread of smoke), object-fit cover (2400×1792 → 1446×1080), object-position 55% 50%, opacity 0 until 3.9 s, pushing 1.00→1.03 from 3.9 to 6.0 s around the panel centre (R.ease.inOut). LEFT (x 120–720): the eyebrow and the two rules, one line each, as a block spanning y 402–678 and centred on 540.

scenes.notes: Both lines are verbatim rule names from the motion map's 'Six rules'. Each rule finishes before its demonstration starts, so the scene obeys what it says: the rule rises, then the mark draws; the second rule rises, then the photo arrives. The mark never spins, scales or pulses. Put no spec IDs, durations or tokens on screen. The same After dark photo also appears small among the mood tiles in scene 09, which is fine. Grain 0: runtime grain is full-frame and would fall on the Linen column. Conventions as in scene 01.

scenes.title: The storefront
scenes.purpose: Depth of proof. The client sees two more real pages in a quiet browser frame, the tales and the moods, carrying the same light and photographs they have just felt.
scenes.visual: Sand ground. A browser window, R.browser(root, {x: 600, y: 212, w: 1200, h: 661}): a Paper #FAF8F3 top bar of 44 px with three hairline dots, a 1 px Dune #CDBFA5 outline, radius 0, no shadow, no URL text. Its viewport is 1200×617 at stage (600, 256). Captures are placed with R.capture(viewport, name, 1440) at scale 0.8333, showing 740 css rows. W1: tales-desktop.scroll(36), showing css 36–776: the header, 'Tales', 'One story per bottle.', its sub-line, and the featured Shadow of the Sea tale (photo, eyebrow, title, excerpt, 'Read the tale'). W2: home-desktop, drifting from css 4700 to 4870. It starts on the site's own '03 / Shop by mood' heading, 'For when you know the feeling but not the notes.' and the six mood tiles. It ends with the heading out of frame and a clean Linen margin above the six tiles (Sea air, Golden hour, After dark, Fresh linen, Warm skin, Wild garden; css 4905–5540), all fully in view; the viewport bottom is at css 5611, above 'Try before you commit' (5665). Windows change by crossfade inside the viewport only (the site's G2); the frame never moves. The left column (x 120–520) holds a fixed eyebrow and one page name per window. There are no index numerals, because the pages carry their own.

scenes.title: Mobile first
scenes.purpose: Proof on the device the direction designs for first: two real mobile pages side by side, one still on the house, one drifting through the tales.
scenes.visual: Sand ground. The left column keeps scene 09's eyebrow in the same place and adds a two-line headline. Two minimal phones sit on the right: R.phone(root, {x, y: 148, h: 784, bezel: 12}), each a Night #171614 body of 375×784 with the runtime's default rounded corners and a 351×760 screen. No notch, buttons, reflections, shadow or outline. Phone A is at x 920 (920–1295); phone B at x 1425 (1425–1800). Screens show R.capture(screen, 'home-mobile', 390) at scale 0.9, with 844 css rows visible. Phone A: scroll(7565), static, showing css 7565–8409: a thin Linen strip, then the Night house band (the house film poster with its play control hidden in the capture, 'THE HOUSE', 'Composed to be remembered.', its paragraph and 'Our story'), then Linen below. It ends before the 'Tales' heading, whose glyphs start at css 8417. Phone B: scroll drifts from 8380 to 9000. It starts on 'Tales', 'All tales' and the Wayne card with its line, and ends on the Enzo 1898 and Forbidden Apple cards with their signature lines (css 9000–9844, above the Join band at 9885).

scenes.title: Never meant to fade
scenes.purpose: Return to the light the film opened on and sign it with the wordmark and the tagline, the promise the whole direction serves. The last frame is the end card that stays on screen for the conversation.
scenes.background: The hero film full-bleed over Night #171614
scenes.visual: The hero film returns full-bleed with the same framing as scene 01: two blended R.film(root, {x: 0, y: 0, w: 1920, h: 1080}) images at τ = t from t = 0 (a seamless 24 fps loop at native speed). The bottle stands at x 1222–1492, y 333–740. Both images push scale 1.00→1.03 over 0–6.4 s (R.ease.inOut), transform-origin 70.8% 50%. Scene 01's left scrim fades in over it: linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(23,22,20,.50) 0%, rgba(23,22,20,.28) 38%, rgba(23,22,20,0) 62%). The wordmark, a short hairline and the tagline sit on the left in the open sea (x 120–805), around the vertical centre (block y 380–678), and never cross the bottle. The hairline is Dune #CDBFA5, 64×1 px, running x 124–188 at y 590. The film keeps breathing under the text to the very last frame. There is no fade to black: the final frame is the end card.

scenes.notes: Grain function: t < 0.9 ? 0 : min(0.035, 0.035·(t − 0.9)/0.6), so no grain lands on scene 10's Sand while the wipe passes. This is the last scene, so it must render its final state at exactly t = 6.4 (the runtime includes the last frame). The wordmark is set as type in the same face as components/ui/Wordmark.tsx: Cormorant Garamond 600, lowercase, tracking 0.02em. Do not add the e∞ mark, a URL, a call to action or any claim. This bookends scene 01 with the same film, framing and scrim; use the frame blending from scene 01's conventions. Conventions as in scene 01.
